name: Chinkhu
description: Chinkhu is a mountain in Nagaland, India.
facts: Listed in geographic records as a mountain in Nagaland
Included because mapped sites often stay off visitor itineraries

name: Kohima
description: Capital city of Nagaland and headquarters of Kohima district, perched on hills at about 1,444 m elevation. Main gateway and base for exploring Angami Naga culture, WWII history, and nearby valleys and peaks.
facts: Connected by road from Dimapur airport/rail (about 74 km)

name: Kohima War Cemetery
description: Commonwealth War Graves Commission cemetery on Garrison Hill commemorating the 1944 Battle of Kohima. Contains 1,420 burials and the historic tennis court where intense fighting occurred; famous for the epitaph 'For your tomorrow, we gave our today'.
facts: Site of the Battle of Kohima tennis court

name: Nagaland State Museum
description: State museum on Bayavü Hill showcasing ethnographic collections of Naga tribes including textiles, ornaments, weapons, musical instruments and replica morungs. Established 1970 under the Department of Art and Culture.
facts: Displays artefacts from all major Naga tribes
Located about 1.5-2 km from town centre

name: Mary Help of Christians Cathedral
description: Catholic cathedral in Kohima with architecture blending traditional Naga house elements. Features one of Asia's largest carved wood crucifixes; consecrated 1991 and partly funded as a memorial related to WWII.

name: Kisama Heritage Village
description: Open-air Naga Heritage Village about 12 km south of Kohima, designed with traditional morungs of the major Naga tribes. Permanent venue of the annual Hornbill Festival (1-10 December).
facts: About 12 km from Kohima on NH
Houses morungs of Naga ethnic groups
Name amalgamates nearby Kigwema and Phesama villages

name: Khonoma Green Village
description: Angami Naga village about 20 km west of Kohima, known as India's first green village for community-led conservation. Features terraced fields, warrior history (1879 resistance), and the Khonoma Nature Conservation and Tragopan Sanctuary protecting Blyth's tragopan.
facts: Terraced paddy fields and historic forts

name: Dzukou Valley
description: High-altitude valley (about 2,438-2,452 m) on the Nagaland-Manipur border behind Japfu Peak, known as the Valley of Flowers of the Northeast. Features rolling meadows, seasonal wildflowers including the Dzukou lily, streams and trekking trails from Viswema or Jakhama.
facts: Famous for seasonal flowers and Dzukou lily

name: Japfu Peak
description: Second-highest peak in Nagaland at 3,048 m in the Barail Range, about 15 km south of Kohima. Popular moderate trek with panoramic views, snow in winter, and the Guinness record tallest rhododendron tree nearby.
facts: Guinness record for tallest rhododendron tree

name: Dzuleke Village
description: Small Angami Naga eco-tourism village about 30-40 km from Kohima, with community ban on hunting. Offers homestays, nature walks, birdwatching (including tragopan habitat) and pristine forests and streams.

name: Touphema Tourist Village
description: Community-based tourist village about 36-41 km from Kohima recreating traditional Angami Naga settlement with huts, cultural performances, local cuisine and a small ethnographic museum. Model for rural tourism.
facts: Cultural dances and Naga food available

name: Pulie Badze Wildlife Sanctuary
description: Protected area of about 9.23 sq km in Kohima district named after the 2,296 m Pulie Badze peak overlooking the capital. Important bird area with Blyth's tragopan, forests and trails; established 1980.
facts: Home to Blyth's tragopan and other birds
